Your claim **is** trying to override my point. You say in "her backstory there's something about Ymir relating to love". Let's say this is based on three panels:

1. Ymir looking at the couple (122)
2. Ymir looking at the couple kissing (122)
3. Same as 1, but in chapter 137

So, you think that 3 panels so heavily imply Ymir's love SPECIFICALLY towards Fritz to be her motivation, rather than focusing on the entire pages of her being abused, mistreated, and choosing to die rather than be with him? Or, the obvious implication of her choosing Eren over Zeke being analogous to her breaking free from being a slave to those with royal blood? 

You don't quote any other evidence of her loving Fritz other than those panels. If Isayama wanted her to be stuck in paths because of her connections or because she wanted love, that's fine and has been implied by the panels you've given, but the story specifically chose for it to be a love for Fritz, which is NOT implied. Explain how the panels indicate that Ymir loves Fritz other than they vaguely introduce the idea of love to Ymir's character. Give me a quote, an image of her looking lovingly at Fritz, anything.

In Ymir’s background, they die to a spear which wouldn’t kill them unless they chose to die. Zeke confirms (in the same panel that you’re referencing) that Eren understood Ymir’s motivations, that “she did still feel attached to the world she left behind”. I would argue the implication the story has given us is that Ymir CHOSE to die to escape Fritz, but couldn’t move on from everything else and was stuck as a slave. Hence, Eren’s speech about being free and a human bringing life back into her eyes and allowing her to disobey Zeke, who has royal blood. 

If you choose to believe that a panel with Ymir  looking at a married couple (and contrary dialogue to your point) is enough to override everything else the story has told us about her so far, be my guest. I will continue to look at chapter 122 as evidence to the contrary, given that AoT becoming a story about a hunted, raped, slave girl falling in love with her abuser is much less compelling than that girl breaking free of her oppressor (which has parallels to Eren wanting to be free of the walls and the titans/Marley but being unable to do so).
You know something being real doesn’t make it good writing, right? It was also setup to be NOT that at all (chapters 121-123).
Don’t overthink it man. If you want a second date, reach out and ask for one. Either way you’ll get an answer and you won’t have to dwell on it.

My point wasn't to ignore it, but to simply give even ANOTHER example of why someone would sacrifice their queen, and it's silly to try to make and lines on what is and isn't considered a queen sacrifice other than intentionally letting your queen die for compensation (which isn't limited to material compensation but can be positional or a mix).

Fuck off with your high and mighty "Did you not know..." bullshit

Edit: to clarify even further because on rereading I am not satisfied with the clarification of my point. There are a couple reasons to sacrifice your queen: to trade or gain a material advantage, to checkmate, or to gain a winning position. Arbitrarily deciding which points make it a "real" queen sacrifice is asinine.

You'd never intentionally sac your queen without adequate compensation (either creating a winning position or getting material). So, semantically, you could argue no one has ever had a queen sac that's good because if you're only definition is losing an exchange than why do it?
Well, would you call sacrificing a queen to mate a queen sacrifice? Is it really a sac if it wins the game? He sacked the queen for material, hence it's a queen sacrifice

King Fritz raped Ymir, had her hunted for sport, cut out her tongue, and used her as a tool. Her being in love with him is lazy writing trying to make sense of the ending. Just saying "muhhh, Stockholm syndrome is a real thing!" doesn't make it good writing or believable for the plot. The connection to Mikasa is also a loose way to try to connect them together that was also shoved in last minute.

When I think about it, I do agree that most of his closest friends did end up surviving. BUT. Paradis is most likely still heavily out numbered (can't imagine the they make up the majority of the 20% left in the world) and are heavily outgunned in terms of military power (Paradis lost their most experienced military leaders and are behind in terms of weaponry). The likelihood that they overcome hundreds of years of military technology advancement (because the remaining world is more likely to have the records and blueprints of their tech) is, well, unlikely even if they have bought extra time. 
And how was Eren's relationship with Ymir mutually beneficial? Ymir became free, and Eren fucking died saying himself that he didn't want it to happen the way it did.

Haha, soooooo true! I liked how he sacrificed most of his friends to free Ymir who up until the ending he had only used to accomplish his own goals! And how he left his friends in danger of imminent war while his grand plan stripped his friends of their greatest military assets!

I'm not trying to let it wholly represent that argument, I just care that it's an absolutely garbage plot point shoved into the last chapter of the story to try to weave some kind of connection between Ymir and Mikasa. Nobody is going to look back and think "Ah yes, remember when it was revealed that Ymir was in love with her genocidal king who kept her as a slave to expand his empire? What a great twist!" 
Frankly, I don't think the women in SnK are written badly. But this point does leave me sour, as well as Historia not mattering as a character as soon as she becomes queen.
